1	# ML Infrastructure Architecture Dataset
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	This dataset describes a complete machine learning infrastructure architecture as a directed graph of system components (nodes) and data/control flows (edges). It covers the full ML lifecycle from data ingestion through model serving and operational monitoring, including cross-cutting concerns like data lineage and version control.
     5	
     6	## Data Source
     7	
     8	### ml_architecture
     9	A graph structure with two arrays: `nodes` and `edges`.
    10	
    11	**Nodes** (9 total):
    12	- `id` (string): unique identifier for the component
    13	- `label` (string): display name, may include sub-labels for technology stack
    14	- `layer` (string): architectural layer — one of data, compute, serving, observability, cross-cutting
    15	- `sub_components` (array of strings): specific technologies or sub-systems within the node
    16	- `criticality` (integer, 1–10): operational criticality score
    17	- `category` (string): visual grouping category — data-layer, compute-layer, serving-layer, observability-layer
    18	
    19	**Edges** (15 total):
    20	- `source` / `target` (string): node IDs
    21	- `flow_type` (string): one of primary, feedback, lineage
    22	- `throughput_gbps` (float): data throughput in gigabits per second, range 0.1–12.5
    23	- `label` (string): short description of what flows along the edge
    24	
    25	## Data Notes
    26	- Throughput values are representative estimates for a mid-scale ML platform
    27	- Criticality scores are subjective team assessments
    28	- The graph contains cycles via feedback edges (monitoring → data platform, monitoring → training cluster)

     2	name: mermaid-tools
     3	description: Extracts Mermaid diagrams from markdown files and generates high-quality PNG images using bundled scripts. Activates when working with Mermaid diagrams, converting diagrams to PNG, extracting diagrams from markdown, or processing markdown files with embedded Mermaid code.
     4	---
     5	
     6	# Mermaid Tools
     7	
     8	## Overview
     9	
    10	This skill enables extraction of Mermaid diagrams from markdown files and generation of high-quality PNG images. The skill bundles all necessary scripts (`extract-and-generate.sh`, `extract_diagrams.py`, and `puppeteer-config.json`) in the `scripts/` directory for portability and reliability.
    11	
    12	## Core Workflow
    13	
    14	### Standard Diagram Extraction and Generation
    15	
    16	Extract Mermaid diagrams from a markdown file and generate PNG images using the bundled `extract-and-generate.sh` script:
    17	
    18	```bash
    19	cd ~/.claude/skills/mermaid-tools/scripts
    20	./extract-and-generate.sh "<markdown_file>" "<output_directory>"
    21	```
    22	
    23	**Parameters:**
    24	- `<markdown_file>`: Path to the markdown file containing Mermaid diagrams
    25	- `<output_directory>`: (Optional) Directory for output files. Defaults to `<markdown_file_directory>/diagrams`
    26	
    27	**Example:**
    28	```bash
    29	cd ~/.claude/skills/mermaid-tools/scripts
    30	./extract-and-generate.sh "/path/to/document.md" "/path/to/output"
    31	```
    32	
    33	### What the Script Does
    34	
    35	1. **Extracts** all Mermaid code blocks from the markdown file
    36	2. **Numbers** them sequentially (01, 02, 03, etc.) in order of appearance
    37	3. **Generates** `.mmd` files for each diagram
    38	4. **Creates** high-resolution PNG images with smart sizing
    39	5. **Validates** all generated PNG files
    40	
    41	### Output Files
    42	
    43	For each diagram, the script generates:
    44	- `01-diagram-name.mmd` - Extracted Mermaid code
    45	- `01-diagram-name.png` - High-resolution PNG image
    46	
    47	The numbering ensures diagrams maintain their order from the source document.
    48	
    49	## Advanced Usage
    50	
    51	### Custom Dimensions and Scaling
    52	
    53	Override default dimensions using environment variables:
    54	
    55	```bash
    56	cd ~/.claude/skills/mermaid-tools/scripts
    57	MERMAID_WIDTH=1600 MERMAID_HEIGHT=1200 ./extract-and-generate.sh "<markdown_file>" "<output_directory>"
    58	```
    59	
    60	**Available variables:**
    61	- `MERMAID_WIDTH` (default: 1200) - Base width in pixels
    62	- `MERMAID_HEIGHT` (default: 800) - Base height in pixels
    63	- `MERMAID_SCALE` (default: 2) - Scale factor for high-resolution output
    64	
    65	### High-Resolution Output for Presentations
    66	
    67	```bash
    68	cd ~/.claude/skills/mermaid-tools/scripts
    69	MERMAID_WIDTH=2400 MERMAID_HEIGHT=1800 MERMAID_SCALE=4 ./extract-and-generate.sh "<markdown_file>" "<output_directory>"
    70	```
    71	
    72	### Print-Quality Output
    73	
    74	```bash
    75	cd ~/.claude/skills/mermaid-tools/scripts
    76	MERMAID_SCALE=5 ./extract-and-generate.sh "<markdown_file>" "<output_directory>"
    77	```
    78	
    79	## Smart Sizing Feature
    80	
    81	The script automatically adjusts dimensions based on diagram type (detected from filename):
    82	
    83	- **Timeline/Gantt**: 2400×400 (wide and short)
    84	- **Architecture/System/Caching**: 2400×1600 (large and detailed)
    85	- **Monitoring/Workflow/Sequence/API**: 2400×800 (wide for process flows)
    86	- **Default**: 1200×800 (standard size)
    87	
    88	Context-aware naming in the extraction process helps trigger appropriate smart sizing.
    89	
    90	## Important Principles
    91	
    92	### Use Bundled Scripts
    93	
    94	**CRITICAL**: Use the bundled `extract-and-generate.sh` script from this skill's `scripts/` directory. All necessary dependencies are bundled together.
    95	
    96	### Change to Script Directory
    97	
    98	Run the script from its own directory to properly locate dependencies (`extract_diagrams.py` and `puppeteer-config.json`):
    99	
   100	```bash
   101	cd ~/.claude/skills/mermaid-tools/scripts
   102	./extract-and-generate.sh "<markdown_file>" "<output_directory>"
   103	```
   104	
   105	Running the script without changing to the scripts directory first may fail due to missing dependencies.
   106	
   107	## Prerequisites Verification
   108	
   109	Before running the script, verify dependencies are installed:
   110	
   111	1. **mermaid-cli**: `mmdc --version`
   112	2. **Google Chrome**: `google-chrome-stable --version`
   113	3. **Python 3**: `python3 --version`
   114	
   115	If any are missing, consult `references/setup_and_troubleshooting.md` for installation instructions.
   116	
   117	## Troubleshooting
   118	
   119	For detailed troubleshooting guidance, refer to `references/setup_and_troubleshooting.md`, which covers:
   120	
   121	- Browser launch failures
   122	- Permission issues
   123	- No diagrams found
   124	- Python extraction failures
   125	- Output quality issues
   126	- Diagram-specific sizing problems
   127	
   128	Quick fixes for common issues:
   129	
   130	**Permission denied:**
   131	```bash
   132	chmod +x ~/.claude/skills/mermaid-tools/scripts/extract-and-generate.sh
   133	```
   134	
   135	**Low quality output:**
   136	```bash
   137	MERMAID_SCALE=3 ./extract-and-generate.sh "<markdown_file>" "<output_directory>"
   138	```
   139	
   140	**Chrome/Puppeteer errors:**
   141	Verify all WSL2 dependencies are installed (see references for full list).
   142	
   143	## Bundled Resources
   144	
   145	### scripts/
   146	
   147	This skill bundles all necessary scripts for Mermaid diagram generation:
   148	
   149	- **extract-and-generate.sh** - Main script that orchestrates extraction and PNG generation
   150	- **extract_diagrams.py** - Python script for extracting Mermaid code blocks from markdown
   151	- **puppeteer-config.json** - Chrome/Puppeteer configuration for WSL2 environment
   152	
   153	All scripts must be run from the `scripts/` directory to properly locate dependencies.
   154	
   155	### references/setup_and_troubleshooting.md
   156	
   157	Comprehensive reference documentation including:
   158	- Complete prerequisite installation instructions
   159	- Detailed environment variable reference
   160	- Extensive troubleshooting guide
   161	- WSL2-specific Chrome dependency setup
   162	- Validation procedures
   163	
   164	Load this reference when dealing with setup issues, installation problems, or advanced customization needs.

1	#!/bin/bash
     2	# Enhanced Mermaid diagram extraction and PNG generation script
     3	# Extracts diagrams from markdown and numbers them sequentially
     4	#
     5	# Usage: ./extract-and-generate.sh <markdown_file> [output_directory]
     6	# Example: ./extract-and-generate.sh "~/workspace/document.md" "~/workspace/diagrams"
     7	
     8	set -e
     9	
    10	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    11	CONFIG_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/puppeteer-config.json"
    12	EXTRACTOR_SCRIPT="$SCRIPT_DIR/extract_diagrams.py"
    13	
    14	# Parse arguments
    15	if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
    16	    echo "Usage: $0 <markdown_file> [output_directory]"
    17	    echo "Example: $0 '~/workspace/document.md' '~/workspace/diagrams'"
    18	    exit 1
    19	fi
    20	
    21	MARKDOWN_FILE="$1"
    22	OUTPUT_DIR="${2:-$(dirname "$MARKDOWN_FILE")/diagrams}"
    23	
    24	echo "=== Enhanced Mermaid Diagram Processor ==="
    25	echo "Source markdown: $MARKDOWN_FILE" 
    26	echo "Output directory: $OUTPUT_DIR"
    27	echo "Environment: WSL2 Ubuntu with Chrome dependencies"
    28	echo
    29	
    30	# Validate inputs
    31	if [ ! -f "$MARKDOWN_FILE" ]; then
    32	    echo "ERROR: Markdown file not found: $MARKDOWN_FILE"
    33	    exit 1
    34	fi
    35	
    36	# Create output directory if it doesn't exist
    37	mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"
    38	
    39	# Configuration
    40	CHROME_PATH="${PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH:-/usr/bin/chromium}"
    41	
    42	# Check dependencies
    43	echo "Checking dependencies..."
    44	if ! command -v mmdc &> /dev/null; then
    45	    echo "ERROR: @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli not installed"
    46	    echo "Install with: npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli"
    47	    exit 1
    48	fi
    49	
    50	if [ ! -f "$CHROME_PATH" ]; then
    51	    echo "ERROR: Google Chrome not found at $CHROME_PATH"
    52	    echo "Install Chrome and dependencies with the setup commands"
    53	    exit 1
    54	fi
    55	
    56	if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
    57	    echo "ERROR: Puppeteer config not found: $CONFIG_FILE"
    58	    exit 1
    59	fi
    60	
    61	if [ ! -f "$EXTRACTOR_SCRIPT" ]; then
    62	    echo "ERROR: Python extractor script not found: $EXTRACTOR_SCRIPT"
    63	    exit 1
    64	fi
    65	
    66	echo "✅ Dependencies verified"
    67	echo
    68	
    69	# Extract Mermaid diagrams from markdown
    70	echo "Extracting Mermaid diagrams from markdown..."
    71	python3 "$EXTRACTOR_SCRIPT" "$MARKDOWN_FILE" "$OUTPUT_DIR"
    72	
    73	if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    74	    echo "ERROR: Failed to extract diagrams from markdown"
    75	    exit 1
    76	fi
    77	
    78	echo
    79	
    80	# Now generate PNGs using the existing generation logic
    81	echo "Generating PNG files..."
    82	cd "$OUTPUT_DIR"
    83	
    84	# Default dimensions - can be overridden with environment variables  
    85	DEFAULT_WIDTH="${MERMAID_WIDTH:-1200}"
    86	DEFAULT_HEIGHT="${MERMAID_HEIGHT:-800}"
    87	SCALE_FACTOR="${MERMAID_SCALE:-2}"
    88	
    89	# Process all .mmd files in order
    90	mmd_files=(*.mmd)
    91	
    92	if [ ${#mmd_files[@]} -eq 1 ] && [ "${mmd_files[0]}" = "*.mmd" ]; then
    93	    echo "No .mmd files found in output directory"
    94	    exit 0
    95	fi
    96	
    97	# Sort files numerically by their prefix
    98	IFS=$'\n' mmd_files=($(sort -V <<< "${mmd_files[*]}"))
    99	
   100	echo "Found ${#mmd_files[@]} Mermaid diagram(s) to process"
   101	echo
   102	
   103	for mmd_file in "${mmd_files[@]}"; do
   104	    if [ ! -f "$mmd_file" ]; then
   105	        continue
   106	    fi
   107	    
   108	    # Extract filename without extension
   109	    diagram="${mmd_file%.mmd}"
   110	    
   111	    # Use smart defaults based on diagram content or filename patterns
   112	    width="$DEFAULT_WIDTH"
   113	    height="$DEFAULT_HEIGHT"
   114	    
   115	    # Smart sizing based on filename patterns
   116	    if [[ "$diagram" =~ timeline|gantt ]]; then
   117	        width=$((DEFAULT_WIDTH * 2))  # Wider for timelines
   118	        height=$((DEFAULT_HEIGHT / 2))  # Shorter for timelines
   119	    elif [[ "$diagram" =~ architecture|system ]]; then
   120	        width=$((DEFAULT_WIDTH * 2))  # Larger for complex diagrams
   121	        height=$((DEFAULT_HEIGHT * 2))
   122	    elif [[ "$diagram" =~ caching ]]; then
   123	        width=$((DEFAULT_WIDTH * 2))  # Larger for caching flowcharts
   124	        height=$((DEFAULT_HEIGHT * 2))
   125	    elif [[ "$diagram" =~ monitoring|workflow|sequence|api ]]; then
   126	        width=$((DEFAULT_WIDTH * 2))  # Wider for workflows and sequences
   127	        height="$DEFAULT_HEIGHT"
   128	    fi
   129	    
   130	    echo "Generating $diagram.png (${width}x${height}, scale: ${SCALE_FACTOR}x)..."
   131	    PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH="$CHROME_PATH" mmdc \
   132	        -i "$mmd_file" \
   133	        -o "$diagram.png" \
   134	        --puppeteerConfigFile "$CONFIG_FILE" \
   135	        -w "$width" \
   136	        -H "$height" \
   137	        -s "$SCALE_FACTOR"

#!/bin/sh
if ! [ -x /snap/bin/chromium ]; then
    echo "" >&2
    echo "Command '$0' requires the chromium snap to be installed." >&2
    echo "Please install it with:" >&2
    echo "" >&2
    echo "snap install chromium" >&2
    echo "" >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [ "$(xdg-settings get default-web-browser)" = "chromium-browser.desktop" ]; then
  xdg-settings set default-web-browser chromium_chromium.desktop
fi

# GNOME Shell
OLD="chromium-browser.desktop"
NEW="chromium_chromium.desktop"
FAVS=$(gsettings get org.gnome.shell favorite-apps 2> /dev/null)
if echo "$FAVS" | grep -q "'$OLD'"; then
  NEWFAVS=$(echo $FAVS | sed -e "s#'$OLD'#'$NEW'#")
  gsettings set org.gnome.shell favorite-apps "$NEWFAVS"
fi

# Unity
OLD="application://chromium-browser.desktop"
NEW="application://chromium_chromium.desktop"
FAVS=$(gsettings get com.canonical.Unity.Launcher favorites 2> /dev/null)
if echo "$FAVS" | grep -q "'$OLD'"; then
  NEWFAVS=$(echo $FAVS | sed -e "s#'$OLD'#'$NEW'#")
  gsettings set com.canonical.Unity.Launcher favorites "$NEWFAVS"
fi

# MATE
OLD="/usr/share/applications/chromium-browser.desktop"
NEW="/var/lib/snapd/desktop/applications/chromium_chromium.desktop"
OBJECTS=$(gsettings get org.mate.panel object-id-list 2> /dev/null)
for object in $OBJECTS; do
  object=$(echo $object | cut -d\' -f2)
  launcher=$(gsettings get org.mate.panel.object:/org/mate/panel/objects/$object/ launcher-location)
  if [ "$launcher" = "'$OLD'" ]; then
    gsettings set org.mate.panel.object:/org/mate/panel/objects/$object/ launcher-location "'$NEW'"
  fi
done

# KDE Plasma
if which qdbus > /dev/null; then
  SCRIPT="$(cat <<-EOF
    for (var i = 0; i < panelIds.length; ++i) {
      var panel = panelById(panelIds[i]);
      var widgets = panel.widgets();
      for (var j = 0; j < widgets.length; ++j) {
        var widget = widgets[j];
        if (widget.type == "org.kde.plasma.taskmanager") {
          widget.currentConfigGroup = "General";
          var launchers = widget.readConfig("launchers");
          if (launchers.includes("chromium-browser.desktop")) {
            widget.writeConfig("launchers", launchers.replace(/chromium-browser.desktop/g, "chromium_chromium.desktop"));
          }
        }
      }
    }
EOF
  )"
  qdbus org.kde.plasmashell /PlasmaShell org.kde.PlasmaShell.evaluateScript "$SCRIPT" 2> /dev/null
fi

# TODO: handle other desktop environments

exec /snap/bin/chromium "$@"
